hero.headline: Read, learn, measure, and steer open-weight models in Rust
hero.metaDescription: Ster is a native Rust toolkit for representation reading and activation steering in local open-weight language models.
hero.lede: Ster is a native Rust toolkit for reading last-token hidden states, learning directions from contrastive examples, evaluating them, and applying measured interventions during generation.

sections.heading: A direction is only valid inside its exact boundary
sections.lede: Representation work breaks when model, layer, width, method, and intervention point drift apart.

items.title: Layer and width must stay explicit
items.text: Ster reads last-token hidden states from selected transformer layers and records hidden width in the artifact.

items.title: Method must travel with the vector
items.text: Artifacts record trait, method, layer-indexed directions, training accuracy, and projection margin.

items.title: The wrong stream is refused
items.text: Ster refuses artifacts with the wrong product, schema, model, or vector width instead of applying them.

sections.heading: One path from contrastive examples to controlled generation
sections.lede: The workflow stays inside one native Rust binary and library crate with versioned JSON artifacts.

items.title: Read
items.text: Ster reads last-token hidden states from selected transformer layers.

items.title: Learn
items.text: Ster learns directions from contrastive examples with CAA, PCA, or logistic-probe training.

items.title: Measure
items.text: Ster evaluates artifacts with pair-ordering accuracy and projection margin, with holdout selection across method and layer.

items.title: Steer
items.text: Ster adds a measured direction in the residual stream during autoregressive generation.

sections.heading: Adoption questions answered by the contract

items.question: Does Ster route hosted models or manage fleets?
items.answer: No. Ster controls local open-weight models; hosted routing, fleet placement, credentials, and release delivery belong to other products.

items.question: What checkpoints can the current runtime use?

items.question: What stops a vector from the wrong model being applied?
items.answer: Ster refuses artifacts with the wrong product, schema, model, or vector width instead of applying them to the wrong residual stream.
